title: Python Oracle Template
description:
# Python Oracle Pattern for LICHEN

## PURPOSE

Python oracles are reference implementations that:
- Parse spec text to extract requirements (MUST/SHALL/SHOULD statements)
- Implement the algorithm in clear, readable Python
- Generate test vectors (JSON) for cross-validation
- Serve as the "source of truth" for Rust/Zephyr implementations

The oracle exists to make the spec executable. When Rust or Zephyr implementations disagree with Python, Python wins unless the spec is wrong.

## STRUCTURE

Each oracle task should have these subtasks:

### a) Parse Spec
- Extract MUST/SHALL/SHOULD statements from the relevant spec section
- Create a checklist of requirements to implement
- Note any ambiguities or underspecified behavior

### b) Implement
- Write Python code in `python/src/lichen/<module>/<feature>.py`
- Code should be clear and readable over fast
- Document spec section references in docstrings
- Use type hints throughout

### c) Generate Vectors
- Output test vectors to `test/vectors/<chapter>-<section>-<name>.json`
- Cover: normal case, edge cases, error cases
- Include intermediate values for debugging
- Vector format must match `test/vectors/README.md` schema

### d) Validate
- Run against any existing test vectors
- Cross-check with RFC examples where available
- Verify round-trip encoding/decoding

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

- [ ] All MUST statements have corresponding code
- [ ] All SHOULD statements documented (implemented or explicitly skipped with rationale)
- [ ] Test vectors cover: normal case, edge cases, error cases
- [ ] Code passes `ruff check` and `pytest`
- [ ] Vector format matches `test/vectors/README.md` schema

## FILE CONVENTIONS

| Type | Path |
|------|------|
| Oracle code | `python/src/lichen/<module>/<feature>.py` |
| Tests | `python/tests/<module>/test_<feature>.py` |
| Vectors | `test/vectors/<chapter>-<section>-<name>.json` |

## WORKFLOW

1. Claim the Python subtask for a spec section
2. Read the spec section, extract requirements
3. Implement the oracle following the structure above
4. Generate test vectors
5. Run quality gates: `ruff check src/ tests/ && pytest`
6. Close the Python subtask
7. Rust/Zephyr implementations can now use your vectors
close_reason: Template complete: Python oracle pattern is established and actively used. Test vectors exist in test/vectors/ (100+ files), oracles in python/src/lichen/, and schema documented in test/vectors/README.md. No implementation work required - this EPIC serves as reference documentation.
